newsitem.title: UK: U.S. Treasuries in London pause before data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries in London pause before data.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were steady on Friday ahead of a stream of data later in the session, after forging ahead in New York, analysts said.
"We are just waiting for the figures," said one trader at a Japanese bank in London. "We are quite overbought but the trend is pretty rock solid."
The 30-year bond was at 104-11 at 0924 GMT to yield 6.299 percent, unchanged from the Tokyo and New York closing levels.

Markets are awaiting the July employment data and June personal income and consumption figures at 1230 GMT. At 1400 GMT is the July National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) report and the final July University of Michigan sentiment index.
Non-farm payrolls will rise by 193,000, according to a Reuters survey, against 217,000 in June.
"We are looking for 220,000," said Adam Chester, international bond strategist at Yamaichi International in London.

"But it would have to be a very strong number to knock the market off its positive momentum. Short of anything above 250,000, the market will continue moving higher. A yield of 6.25 percent on the long bond is the target," he added.
September T-bond futures were at 116-23 in automated trade at 0931 GMT, down 1/32 from the Chicago pit close. December Eurodollars were up 0.005 at 94.220.
